nodes.raw_latex:
\label{ass_g_poi} The objective function $g(\theta)$ satisfies the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item\label{ass_g_poi:i} $g(\theta)$ is continuously differentiable and non-negative.
\item\label{ass_g_poi:i2} $\nabla g(\theta)$ is Lipschitz continuous, i.e., $
\big\|\nabla g(\theta)-\nabla g(\theta')\big\|\le L\|\theta-\theta'\| $, for all $\theta, \theta' \in \mathbb{R}^{d}$.
\item\label{ass_g_poi:i3}(\textbf{Only for asymptotic convergence}) $g(\theta)$ is not asymptotically flat, i.e., there exists $\eta>0$ such that $\liminf_{\|\theta\|\rightarrow+\infty} \|\nabla g(\theta)\|^{2}>\eta.$

\end{enumerate}

nodes.statement: Since the critical point set J is bounded, the critical values set f(J_f) is closed. Suppose that there exists an interval (a, b) such that the set f(J_f) is dense on this interval. This condition is both necessary and sufficient to guarantee f(J_f) to have an interior point. Given that f is d-times differentiable, we can apply Sard's theorem citepsard1942measure,bates1993toward and deduce that m(f(J_f))=0, where m(cdot) denotes Lebesgue's Measure. It is well known that a set containing an interior point cannot have a zero measure. Thus, we conclude that f(J_f) is nowhere dense in R.

\label{SA_p}
Let $F$ be a continuous globally integrable vector field. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(A.\arabic*)},leftmargin=*]
    \item\label{pros:a1} Suppose $\sup_n \|x_n\|< \infty,$ 
    \item\label{pros:a2} For all $T > 0$
    \[
    \lim_{n \to \infty} \sup \left\lbrace \left\lVert \sum_{i=n}^{k} \gamma_{i}U_{i} \right\lVert : k = n, \dots, m(\Sigma_{\gamma}(n) + T) \right\rbrace = 0,
    \]
    where 
    \[\Sigma_\gamma(n):=\sum_{k=1}^{n}\gamma_{k}\ \ \text{and}\ \ m(t):=\max\{j\ge 0:  \Sigma_{\gamma}(j)\le t\}.\] 
    \item\label{pros:a3} \(F(V)\) is nowhere dense on \(\mathbb{R}\), where \(V\) is the fixed point set of the ODE: \(\dot{x} = g(x)\).

\end{enumerate}
Then all limit points of the sequence \(\{x_{n}\}_{n\ge 1}\) are fixed points of the ODE: \(\dot{x} = g(x)\).

Meanwhile, Theorem 5.7 and Proposition 6.4 demonstrate that all limit points of this precompact asymptotic pseudotrajectory are fixed points of the ODE system.

To illustrate this concept, let us consider a sequence of random variables \zeta_n\_nge 1, where P[zeta_n=0]=1-1/n^2 and P[zeta_n=n^2]=1/n^2. According to the Borel-Cantelli lemma, it follows that lim_nrightarrow+inftyzeta_n=0 almost surely. However, it can be shown that E[zeta_n]=1 for all n>0 by simple calculations.

(Almost-sure vs mean-square convergence)
As stated in the introduction, the almost sure convergence does not imply mean square convergence. To illustrate this concept, let us consider a sequence of random variables $\{\zeta_{n}\}_{n\ge 1},$ where $\mathbb{P}[\zeta_{n}=0]=1-1/n^{2}$ and $\mathbb{P}[\zeta_{n}=n^{2}]=1/n^{2}.$ According to \textit{the Borel-Cantelli lemma}, it follows that $\lim_{n\rightarrow+\infty}\zeta_{n}=0$ almost surely. However, it can be shown that $\mathbb{E}[\zeta_{n}]=1$ for all $n>0$ by simple calculations.

\label{vital2}(Burkholder's inequality)
Let \( \{X_n\}_{n \geq 0} \) be a real-valued martingale difference sequence for a filtration \( \{\mathscr{F}_n\}_{n \geq 0} \), and let \( s\le t<+\infty \) be two stopping time with respect to the same filtration \( \{\mathscr{F}_n\}_{n \geq 0} \). Then for any \( p > 1 \), there exist positive constants \( C_p \) and \( C_p' \) (depending only on \( p \)) such that 
\[C_p \mathbb{E}\left[\bigg(\sum_{n=s}^{t}|X_{n}|^{2}\bigg)^{p/2}\right] \leq \mathbb{E}\left[\sup_{s \leq n \leq t} \bigg|\sum_{k=s}^{n}X_k\bigg|^{p} \right] \leq C_p' \mathbb{E}\left[\bigg(\sum_{n=s}^{t}|X_{n}|^{2}\bigg)^{p/2}\right].\]

\label{vital1}(Doob's stopped theorem)
For an adapted process $(Y_{n}, \mathscr{F}_{n})$, if there exist two bounded stopping times $s \leq t < +\infty\ a.s.$, and if $[s= n] \in \mathscr{F}_{n-1}$ and $[t=n]\in \mathscr{F}_{n-1}$ for all $n > 0$, then the following equation holds.
\[
\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n=s}^{t}Y_{n}\right] = \mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{n=s}^{t}\mathbb{E}[Y_{n}|\mathscr{F}_{n-1}]\right].
\]

nodes.statement: (of creflem:estimation:supg) For any Tgeq 1, we calculate \(Eleft(sup_n ge 1 g(theta_n)right)\) based on the segment of g on the stopping time & EBig[sup_1le n<Tg(theta_n)Big] notag \\&le EBig[sup_1le n< tau_1,Tg(theta_n)Big] +EBig[sup_tau_1,Tle n<Tg(theta_n)Big]notag\\&=EBig[I_[tau_1,T=1]sup_1le n< tau_1,Tg(theta_n)Big]+underbraceEBig[I_[tau_1,T>1]sup_1le n< tau_1,Tg(theta_n)Big]_Pi_1, T +underbraceEBig[sup_tau_1,Tle n< Tg(theta_n)Big]_Pi_2,Tnotag\\&mathople^(a)0+Delta_0+Pi_2,T, where we define tau_t,T:=tau_twedge T. To make the inequality consistent, we let sup_a le t < b(cdot) = 0 \ (forall\ a ge b). For (a) in crefstart, since tau_1,T geq 1, we have EBig[I_[tau_1,T=1]sup_1le n< tau_1,Tg(theta_n)Big]=0 and Pi_1, T&=EBig[I_[tau_1,T>1]sup_1le n< tau_1,Tg(theta_n)Big]leEBig[I_[tau_1>1]sup_1le n< tau_1,Tg(theta_n)Big]leDelta_0. Next, we focus on Pi_2,T. Specifically, we have: Pi_T,2&=EBig[sup_tau_1,Tle n<Tg(theta_n)Big]=Ebigg[sup_ige 1Big(sup_tau_3i-2,Tle n<tau_3i+1,Tg(theta_n)Big)bigg]notag\\&leunderbraceEbigg[Big(sup_tau_1,Tle n<tau_4,Tg(theta_n)Big)bigg]_Pi_2,T^1+underbraceEbigg[sup_ige 2Big(sup_tau_3i-2,Tle n<tau_3i+1,Tg(theta_n)Big)bigg]_Pi_2,T^2. We decompose Pi_2,T into Pi_2,T^1 and Pi_2,T^2 and estimate them separately. For the term Pi_2,T^1 we have Pi_2,T^1& = Ebigg[Big(sup_tau_1,Tle n<tau_3,Tg(theta_n)Big)bigg]+Ebigg[Big(sup_tau_3,Tle n<tau_4,Tg(theta_n)Big)bigg] notag \\ & mathople^creffab_2 Ebigg[Big(sup_tau_1,Tle n<tau_3,Tg(theta_n)Big)bigg]+Delta_0notag\\&=E[g(theta_tau_1,T)]+Ebigg[Big(sup_tau_1,Tle n<tau_3,T(g(theta_n)-g(theta_tau_1,T))Big)bigg]+Delta_0notag\\ &=E[I_[tau_1=1]g(theta_tau_1)]+E[I_[tau_1>1]g(theta_tau_1)]+Ebigg[Big(sup_tau_1,Tle n<tau_3,T(g(theta_n)-g(theta_tau_1,T))Big)bigg]+Delta_0notag\\&mathople^(a)g(theta_1)+Big(Delta_0+alpha_0sqrt2 LDelta_0+frac Lalpha_0^22Big)+Ebigg[Big(sup_tau_1,Tle n<tau_3,T(g(theta_n)-g(theta_tau_1,T))Big)bigg] + Delta_0notag\\&mathople^(b)g(theta_1)+2Delta_0+alpha_0sqrt2 LDelta_0+frac Lalpha_0^22 + C_Pi,1 EBigg[sum_n=tau_1,T^tau_3,T-1 zeta(n)Bigg], where C_Pi,1 is a constant and is defined in crefinqu:diff:g:tau1. For (a) of crefinequ:xt21, we follow the fact that EBig[I_[tau_1,T>1]g(theta_tau_1,T-1)Big]le Delta_0 and get that E[I_[tau_1>1]g(theta_tau_1,T)]&=E[I_[tau_1>1]g(theta_tau_1,T-1)]+E[I_[tau_1>1]g(theta_tau_1,T)-g(theta_tau_1,T-1)]\\&mathople^crefinequ:g:adj Delta_0+alpha_0sqrt2 LDelta_0+frac Lalpha_0^22. For (b) we use the one-step iterative formula on g g(theta_n+1)-g(theta_n)&le nabla g(theta_n)^top(theta_n+1-theta_n)+frac L2\|theta_n+1-theta_n\|^2 notag \\&lefracalpha_0\|nabla g(theta_n)\|\|nabla g(theta_n,xi_n)\|sqrtS_n+frac Lalpha_0^22frac\|nabla g(theta_n,xi_n)\|^2S_n notag \\ & leq fracalpha_0\|nabla g(theta_n)\|sqrtS_n-1 \|nabla g(theta_n,xi_n)\|+frac Lalpha_0^22frac\|nabla g(theta_n,xi_n)\|^2sqrtS_0sqrtS_n-1, which induces that (recall that zeta_n = \|nabla g(theta_n,xi_n)\|^2/sqrtS_n-1) & Ebigg[Big(sup_tau_1,Tle n<tau_3,T(g(theta_n)-g(theta_tau_1,T))Big)bigg] le EBigg[sum_n=tau_1,T^tau_3,T-1|g(theta_n+1)-g(theta_n)|Bigg] notag\\& le EBigg[sum_n=tau_1,T^tau_3,T-1fracalpha_0\|nabla g(theta_n)\|cdot\|nabla g(theta_n,xi_n)\|sqrtS_n-1Bigg]+EBigg[sum_n=tau_1,T^tau_3,T-1frac Lalpha^2_0\|nabla g(theta_n,xi_n)\|^22sqrtS_0sqrtS_n-1Bigg] notag \\&mathop=^(a)Eleft[sum_n=tau_1,T^tau_3,T-1fracalpha_0\|nabla g(theta_n)\|sqrtS_nEleft(\|nabla g(theta_n,xi_n)\| mid F_n-1right)+frac Lalpha_0^22sqrtS_0sum_n=tau_1,T^tau_3,T-1fracE left(\|nabla g(theta_n,xi_n)\|^2 mid F_n-1right) sqrtS_n-1right] notag \\&mathople^(*)bigg(alpha_0Big(sqrtsigma_0+sqrtfracsigma_1etaBig)+frac Lalpha_0^22sqrtS_0Big(sigma_0+fracsigma_1etaBig)bigg)EBigg[sum_n=tau_1,T^tau_3,T-1zeta(n)Bigg] := C_Pi,1EBigg[sum_n=tau_1,T^tau_3,T-1zeta(n)Bigg], where (a) uses crefsum:expect:ab. If tau_1,T > tau_3,T - 1, inequality (*) trivially holds since sum_n=tau_1,T^tau_3,T-1cdot=0. Moving forward we will exclusively examine the case tau_1,T le tau_3,T - 1. By the definition of tau_t, we have hatg(theta_n) > Delta_0 geq hatC_g for any n in [tau_1,T, tau_3,T). Consequently, upon applying crefpro_0, we deduce that \|nabla g(theta_n)\|^2 > eta for any n in [tau_1,T, tau_3,T). Combined with the affine noise variance condition, we further achieve the subsequent inequalities that for any nin[tau_1,T,tau_3,T) E[\|nabla g(theta_n,xi_n)\|^2|F_n-1]&le sigma_0\|nabla g(theta_n)\|^2+sigma_1 < Big(sigma_0+fracsigma_1etaBig)cdot\|nabla g(theta_n)\|^2 and & E[\|nabla g(theta_n,xi_n)\||F_n-1] leq left(E[\|nabla g(theta_n,xi_n)\|^2|F_n-1) right]^1/2 leq Big(sigma_0\|nabla g(theta_n)\|^2+sigma_1Big)^1/2 notag \\ &le sqrtsigma_0\|nabla g(theta_n)\|+sqrtsigma_1 <Big(sqrtsigma_0+sqrtfracsigma_1etaBig)cdot\|nabla g(theta_n)\|. Next, we turn to estimate Pi_2,T^2. Pi_2,T^2&=Ebigg[sup_ige 2Big(sup_tau_3i-2,Tle n<tau_3i+1,Tg(theta_n)Big)bigg]notag\\&le Ebigg[sup_ige 2Big(sup_tau_3i-2,Tle n<tau_3i-1,Tg(theta_n)Big)bigg]+Ebigg[sup_ige 2Big(sup_tau_3i-1,Tle n<tau_3i,Tg(theta_n)Big)bigg]notag\\& +Ebigg[sup_ige 2Big(sup_tau_3i,Tle n<tau_3i+1,Tg(theta_n)Big)bigg]notag\\&mathople^(a) 2Delta_0+Ebigg[sup_ige 2Big(sup_tau_3i-1,Tle n<tau_3i,Tg(theta_n)Big)bigg]+Delta_0notag\\&le 3Delta_0+EBig[sup_n=tau_3i-1,Tg(theta_n)Big]+EBig[sup_ige 2sup_tau_3i-1,Tle nle tau_3i,T(g(theta_n)-g(theta_tau_3i-1,T))Big]notag\\&mathople^(b)3Delta_0+Big(2Delta_0+2alpha_0sqrt LDelta_0+frac Lalpha_0^22Big) + C_Pi,1EBigg[sum_i=2^+inftysum_tau_3i-1,T^tau_3i,T-1zeta(n)Bigg], where (a) follows from creffab_2 and creffabulous. To derive (b), we first use the following estimation of g(theta_n) at the stopping time tau_3i-1,T sup_n=tau_3i-1,Tg(theta_n)&=sup_n=tau_3i-1,Tg(theta_n-1)+sup_n=tau_3i-1,T(g(theta_n)-g(theta_n-1))\\&mathople^crefinequ:g:adj 2Delta_0+2alpha_0sqrt LDelta_0+frac Lalpha_0^22. Then, since the objective g(theta_n) in the interval n in [tau_3i-1,T,tau_3i,T) has similar properties as the interval [tau_1,T,tau_3,T), we follow the same procedure as crefinqu:diff:g:tau1 to estimate the supremum of g(theta_n)-g(theta_tau_3i-1,T) on the interval n in [tau_3i-1,T, tau_3i,T), it achieves that & E left[sup_ige 2sup_tau_3i-1,Tle nle tau_3i,T(g(theta_n)-g(theta_tau_3i-1,T))right] leq E left[sum_i=2^+inftysup_tau_3i-1,Tle nle tau_3i,T(g(theta_n)-g(theta_tau_3i-1,T))right] notag \\ & leq bigg(alpha_0Big(sqrtsigma_0+sqrtfracsigma_1etaBig)+frac Lalpha_0^22sqrtS_0Big(sigma_0+fracsigma_1etaBig)bigg)EBigg[sum_i=2^+inftysum_n=tau_3i-1,T^tau_3i,T-1zeta(n)Bigg]. By substituting the estimations of Pi_2,T^1 and Pi_2,T^2 from crefinequ:xt21 and crefqaswert respectively into crefinequ:xt2, we achieve the estimation for Pi_2,T. Then, substituting the result for Pi_2,T into crefstart gives EBig[sup_1le n<Tg(theta_n)Big]le C_Pi,0+C_Pi, 1underbraceEBigg[sum_n=tau_1,T^tau_3,T-1zeta(n)+sum_i=2^+inftysum_tau_3i-1,T^tau_3i,T-1zeta(n)Bigg]_Pi_3,T, where C_Pi,0&=g(theta_1)+6Delta_0+5alpha_0sqrt LDelta_0+frac3 Lalpha_0^22, C_Pi,1=alpha_0Big(sqrtsigma_0+sqrtfracsigma_1etaBig)+frac Lalpha_0^22sqrtS_0Big(sigma_0+fracsigma_1etaBig). Next, we turn to find an upper bound for Pi_3,T which is independent of T. Recall the sufficient decrease inequality in crefsufficient:lem hatg(theta_n+1)-hatg(theta_n) & le -fracalpha_04zeta_n+C_Gamma,1cdot Gamma_n +C_Gamma,2fracGamma_nsqrtS_n + alpha_0 hatX_n. First, we estimate the first term of Pi_3,T. Telescoping the above inequality over n from the interval \(I_1,tau:=[tau_1,T,tau_3,T-1]\) gives fracalpha_04sum_n in I_1,tauzeta(n)&le hatg(theta_tau_1,T)-hatg(theta_tau_3,T)+C_Gamma,1sum_n in I_1,tau Gamma_n+C_Gamma,2sum_n in I_1,taufracGamma_nsqrtS_n+alpha_0 sum_n in I_1,tauhatX_n. Taking the expectation on both sides of the above inequality, we have fracalpha_04Eleft[sum_n in I_1,tauzeta(n)right]&leEbig[hatg(theta_tau_1,T)big]+C_Gamma,1Ebigg[sum_n in I_1,tau Gamma_n bigg]+C_Gamma,2EBigg[sum_n in I_1,taufracGamma_nsqrtS_nBigg]+alpha_0EBigg[sum_n in I_1,tauhatX_nBigg]notag\\&mathople^(a) Ebig[hatg(theta_tau_1,T)big]+C_Gamma,1Ebigg[sum_n in I_1,tau E[Gamma_n|F_n-1]bigg]+C_Gamma,2EBigg[sum_n in I_1,taufracGamma_nsqrtS_nBigg]+0, where for (a), we use Doob's Stopped theorem (see crefvital1) since the stopping times tau_1,Tle tau_3,T-1 and hatX_n is a martingale sequence. For the first term of the RHS of the above inequality, Ebig[hatg(theta_tau_1,T)big]&=Ebig[I_[tau_1=1]hatg(theta_1)big]+Ebig[I_tau_1>1hatg(theta_tau_1,T)big] \\&le hatg(theta_1)+ Ebig[I_tau_1>1hatg(theta_tau_1,T-1)big]+Ebig[I_tau_1>1(hatg(theta_tau_1,T)-hatg(theta_tau_1,T-1))big]\\&mathople^creflem:adj:ghat hatg(theta_1)+Delta_0+h(Delta_0)<hatg(theta_1)+frac3Delta_02. We thus conclude that fracalpha_04Eleft[sum_n in I_tau,1zeta(n)right]&lehatg(theta_1)+frac3Delta_02+C_Gamma,1Ebigg[sum_n in I_tau,i E[Gamma_n|F_n-1] bigg]+C_Gamma,2EBigg[sum_n in I_tau,ifracGamma_nsqrtS_nBigg]. For the second term of Pi_3,T, we telescope the sufficient decrease inequality in crefsufficient:lem over n from the interval \( I_i,tau^':= [tau_3i-1,T, tau_3i,T-1 ]\ (forall\ ige 2)\) fracalpha_04sum_n in I_i,tau^'zeta(n)&le hatg(theta_tau_3i-1,T)-hatg(theta_tau_3i,T)+C_Gamma,1sum_n in I_i,tau^' Gamma_n+C_Gamma,2sum_n in I_i,tau^'fracGamma_nsqrtS_n+alpha_0 sum_n in I_i,tau^'hatX_n. Recalling the definition of the stopping time tau_t, we know that \(tau_3i,T geq tau_3i-1,T\) always holds. In particular, \(tau_3i,T = tau_3i-1,T\) implies that \(tau_3i,T-1 < tau_3i-1,T\). Since sum_n=a^b(cdot) = 0 for b < a, we have sum_n=tau_3i-1,T^tau_3i,T-1(cdot) = 0 and hatg(theta_tau_3i,T) = hatg(theta_tau_3i-1,T), then LHS and RHS of crefinequ:stab:2 are both zero and crefinequ:stab:2 holds. Taking the expectation on both sides and noting the equation of crefsum:expect:ab gives fracalpha_04Eleft[sum_n in I_i,tau^'zeta(n)right]&le Ebig[hatg(theta_tau_3i-1,T)-hatg(theta_tau_3i,T)big]+C_Gamma,1Ebigg[sum_n in I_i,tau^' E[Gamma_n|F_n-1] bigg]notag\\&+C_Gamma,2EBigg[sum_n in I_i,tau^'fracGamma_nsqrtS_nBigg]+0. If \(tau_3i-1, T < tau_3i, T\), for any n in I_i,tau^' = [tau_3i-1,T, tau_3i,T-1], by applying creflem:adj:ghat we have hatg(theta_tau_3i-1, T) - hatg(theta_tau_3i,T)&<hatg(theta_tau_3i-1,T) < hatg(theta_tau_3i-1,T-1)+h(hatg(theta_tau_3i-1,T-1)). Based on the properties of the stopping time \(tau_3i-1,\) we have hatg(theta_tau_3i-1,T-1) leq 2Delta_0. Based on the above inequality, we further estimate the first term of crefinequ:stat:1 and achieve that fracalpha_04EBigg[sum_n=I_i,tau^'zeta(n)Bigg]notag&le C_Delta_0Ebig[I_\tau_3i-1,T<tau_3i,T \big]+C_Gamma,1Ebigg[sum_n=I_i,tau^' E[Gamma_n|F_n-1] bigg] \\&+C_Gamma,2EBigg[sum_n=I_i,tau^'fracGamma_nsqrtS_nBigg] , where C_Delta_0: =2Delta_0+ sqrt2 Lleft(1 + fracsigma_0 L2sqrtS_0right)alpha_0sqrt2Delta_0 + left(1 + fracsigma_0alpha_0 L2sqrtS_0right)frac Lalpha_0^22.
